Provenance, field by field. PRICES and stated_expiry come from the act itself, read as a PDF at minfin.gov.by/upload/dragmet/gosfond/actual_fizlitca.pdf (appendix Table 1; point 3 reads 'Настоящее постановление вступает в силу после его официального опубликования и действует по 31 июля 2026 г.'). Note that URL is a rolling one - 'actual' - and will point at the successor act once one is published, so it is not a stable citation for this act. ACT_NUMBER and ACT_DATE come only from the appendix heading on the prices page, '08.07.2026 № 31'; the PDF is the unsigned publication form, with both the number and the date fields left blank. EFFECTIVE_FROM is stated twice by the Ministry itself: on the prices page directly above Table 1 ('Вступает в силу с 18 июля 2026 года') and in the news headline 'Цены ... с 18 июля 2026 г.'. It is deliberately not the act date. 08.07.2026 is when the Minister signed it; the act defers its own commencement to official publication, which is a separate and later event (inclusion in the National Legal Register). Point 2 of the act corroborates the gap: it repeals resolution № 27 of 18.06.2026, and that repeal only takes effect when this act does, so № 27 governed 8-17 July and the two do not overlap. The prices were confirmed twice, from the PDF and from the HTML table, independently. KNOWN SOURCE CONFLICT on effective_from, found on 29 July 2026 and unresolved. Once № 31 was superseded it moved to the year archive at minfin.gov.by/ru/activities_jewels/fund/pokupka/fizlic/archive/2026/, and that page dates the same act - identical number, identical date, identical prices - from '17 июля 2026 года', one day earlier. Two Ministry pages disagree by a day. 2026-07-18 is kept because it is the value the Ministry published on the page cited in source_url while the act was actually governing transactions, and the news announcement agrees. The likeliest explanation is that one page states the publication date and the other the day commencement follows it, but that cannot be confirmed without the act's National Register entry, which needs an ЭТАЛОН subscription. Anyone importing history from the archive pages should know they are not always digit-identical to what the live page said at the time. Prices are unaffected: the archive's Table 1 for № 31 matches this record exactly.

notes: The successor to № 31, read on 29 July 2026 while it was still future-dated. Two things differ structurally from № 31 and both are deliberate here. (1) EFFECTIVE_FROM comes from the act itself this time: point 2 reads 'Настоящее постановление вступает в силу 1 августа 2026 г.' - a named date, not a reference to publication. The prices page agrees: 'Вступает в силу с 1 августа 2026 года'. (2) STATED_EXPIRY is null because the act contains no 'действует по' clause at all. № 31 had one; this one simply does not, so it stays in force until an act replaces it. That is a real property of the act, not a gap in transcription - do not fill it in with a guess. There is also no repeal clause, because № 31 ends by its own terms on 31 July. PRICES are from the appendix, Table 1, confirmed twice: from the PDF (layout extraction) and from the HTML table on the prices page, independently, digit for digit. Note 583 and 585 share a single merged cell reading 202,50 - one value covering two finenesses, exactly as in № 31 - so eight numbers cover nine finenesses. ACT_NUMBER and ACT_DATE come from the appendix heading '28.07.2026 № 34'; the PDF leaves its own number and date fields blank. Unrelated to the scrap table but worth recording: point 1 lowers the Белскупдрагмет bullion surcharges to 4.5 per cent for gold and 2.5 for silver, from 5.5 and 4.5 in № 31. VERIFIED. On 30 July 2026 the repository owner compared all nine Table 1 prices in this record against the act on the Ministry page and confirmed they match.
